title: Repair fixed-pilot Examiner gateway authentication without optional secrets
problem: Every current fixed-pilot independent quality judgment fails before gateway execution because it sends a provider key as its bearer and the optional integration-token binding is absent. The existing gateway accepts the already available server service credential.
expected_behavior: Release 5eb1f2c84086db4a067b484cd3de7c5ce6cec182; manifest 52e99810ee1d610c794bc9628b89fd3d19240739045ae12f59b63dec0bd512d4. Only sandy-examiner-full-cycle changes from observed version 13, using its existing server service identity for the normal fixed gateway contract. No other function, channel, pilot or model policy is changed.
change_purpose: Unblock real post-canary independent quality testing using existing valid credentials and normal gateway authorization.
feature_improvement: Remove an unnecessary caller-side provider-key dependency, preserve the existing fixed model/prompt and retain failed/incomplete/malformed judgments as needs_review with redacted failure stages.
regression_rules: Preserve the registered consenting pilot, OIDC workflow restrictions, model and prompt and token budget.
Do not issue customer/owner tokens, add an integration secret or broaden gateway/Controller permissions.
Retain historical quality failures; never claim an incomplete or failed judge as a pass.
Hold the existing component lease and reject changed deployed source/version.
acceptance_criteria: 18 focused tests and offline entrypoint type check pass; verify all three transitive local modules against the immutable manifest.
Verify the existing full-pilot workflow executes actual judgments without the former gateway-auth denial; classify other failures explicitly.
Capture v13 rollback source and preserve V4/workspace source, customer data and all communications.
